In May, you spent **$559.46** across three transactions at Costco ($501.23 across two warehouse grocery visits and $58.23 on gas), all charged to your Chase Sapphire Preferred.

Here are the highest-impact ways to optimize your Costco spend:

### 1. Fix the card rewards gap
Because Costco codes as a wholesale club (MCC 5300) rather than a supermarket, your Chase Sapphire Preferred earns only **1x points (1%)** on warehouse and gas purchases. 
- **Costco Anywhere Visa by Citi ($0 annual fee with membership)**: Earns **5% on Costco gas** (up to $7,000/year shared gas cap, then 1%) and **2% on Costco wholesale purchases**.
- **Alternative flat 2% Visa**: A no-fee 2% cash-back Visa (like the Fidelity Rewards Visa) gets 2% across all warehouse spend with flexible monthly cash redemption.

### 2. Run the Executive Membership math
Costco's Executive tier adds a 2% annual reward on eligible warehouse and online purchases.
- **The breakeven**: Upgrading from Gold Star ($65/yr) to Executive ($130/yr) costs an extra $65. You break even at **$3,250/year** ($271/month) in qualified spend.
- **Your pace**: If your observed warehouse grocery spend of $501.23/month continues, that is roughly $6,015/year—generating about **$120/year in Executive rewards** ($55 net after covering the upgrade cost).
- **Zero-risk downgrade**: If your 2% check ends up under $65 before renewal, Costco will refund the difference upon request at customer service.

### 3. Learn the price tag markdown codes
When browsing the aisles, look at the cents on the tag to spot clearance versus everyday pricing:
- **.99 ending**: Standard everyday corporate price (not discounted).
- **.97 ending**: Manager clearance markdown.
- **.49, .79, .89 endings**: Temporary manufacturer promotional discounts.
- **.00 or .88 endings**: Deep manager markdowns on display, return, or final inventory units.
- **Asterisk (\*) in the top-right corner**: Discontinued item that will not be restocked.
